page: Microsoft Azure E4d_v4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the EDv4 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an Intel Xeon 8272CL processor with a base clock speed of 2.6 GHz. The configuration includes 4 dedicated vCPUs derived from 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. Memory capacity is 32.0 GB, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. Additionally, the instance is equipped with 154 GB of local SSD storage, while no GPUs are present.

Performance benchmarks indicate a clear distinction between single-core and multi-core capabilities. Single-core performance is moderate, with stress-ng single-core and Geekbench single-core scores falling into the average category. However, multi-core and memory bandwidth metrics show limitations. Multi-core CPU performance in stress-ng and Geekbench is categorized as weak, and large-block memory read bandwidth is poor at 22.87 GB/sec. Database operations, Redis SET performance, and static web serving throughput also register in the weak category, reflecting the constraints of the 2-core physical layout under concurrent workloads.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the E4d_v4 offers a high memory-to-vCPU density, making it suitable for memory-intensive workloads that do not require high parallel compute scaling. The inclusion of 154 GB of local storage provides a cost-effective option for temporary data caching without needing external storage attachments. This server is best suited for relational databases with moderate transaction volumes, memory-cached applications, and lightweight enterprise workloads requiring a larger memory footprint relative to processing power.
